newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. offering tariff cuts at APEC - Kyodo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. offering tariff cuts at APEC - Kyodo.

text.p: The United States might be willing to cut tariffs on some products in exchange for APEC's endorsement of a global information technology agreement, Kyodo News Agency reported on Wednesday.

Philippine Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon told Kyodo in an interview on Wednesday that U.S. officials have indicated they might be able to lower tariffs on 15 to 19 items where the executive branch of government alone has the right to make the cuts.
Most U.S. tariffs are subject to approval by Congress.
Siazon said the Philippines wanted lower U.S. tariffs on furniture, wood products and electronics.
"(The U.S.) might still improve their tariff reduction .... in exchange for support (on the informational technology agreement)" Kyodo quoted Siazon as saying.

The United States wants the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum to issue a statement at its summit in Manila next week calling for the forging, in the World Trade Organization (WTO), of a global agreement to eliminate tariffs on information technology products by the year 2000.
Siazon said the Philippines would support the proposed information technology agreement but that support would depend on the speed of tariff cuts and products to be covered.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
